text: Intoxication [Lat. intoxicatus , poisoned]: Ger. Berauschung ; Fr. enivrement ; Ital. intossicazione . (1) The effects of certain drugs or poisons. (2) Frequently limited to alcoholic intoxication. The state of intoxication usually makes itself felt soon after the absorption of the toxic substance. The mental symptoms which characterize it differ considerably according to the poison used; but a very typical characteristic is a state of excitement, release of inhibition, unrestrained conduct, inactivity, exaltation, incoherence. But these are only the characteristics outwardly most conspicuous; effects often differing from those just mentioned, and extending into less obvious alteration in mental processes, characterize the various forms of drug intoxication. These are described in general, and with regard to the more important intoxicants, under PSYCHIC EFFECT OF DRUGS. For the effects produced by alcohol, see ALCOHOLISM. For further details consult the works cited under those topics. ( J.J. )
